Jordan (solutions): quick flag on the Nova POC — Splunk shows request_id but no trace_id/traceparent in indexed events. Anyone seen this?
Priya (sales-eng): Yep. Usually either (a) an intermediary (WAF/sidecar/nginx) strips headers, or (b) forwarder dropped span events during a HEC 429 window.
Jordan (solutions): ALB logs include traceparent and x-nova-trace, but Splunk doesn't. We saw forwarder 429s around 23:12.
Theo (infra): If ALB has it but nginx access_log doesn't, likely WAF or sidecar. If nginx has it but forwarder doesn't, check remap/transforms on the forwarder. Quick non-invasive options: 1) set client to send x-request-id (WAF-friendly) and remap to trace_id in forwarder, or 2) synthesize trace_id from request_id in the forwarder as a POC fallback.
Priya (sales-eng): Customer can't change WAF rules during business hours. They prefer forwarder remap for the short-term. Any sample we can give them?
Theo (infra): Vector remap example: ` .trace_id = if exists(.headers["x-nova-trace"]) { .headers["x-nova-trace"] } else if exists(.headers["x-request-id"]) { .headers["x-request-id"] } else null `
And fallback synth (lua): `if not event.trace_id and event.request_id then event.trace_id = event.request_id end`.
ingest-bot: alert: forwarder.nova.hec 429 spike detected 2026-03-20T23:10Z -> 30m (avg 8/min)
Jordan (solutions): After applying the remap and bumping forwarder buffer (FORWARDER_BUFFER_BYTES=100MB, FORWARDER_RETRIES=5) we see trace_id in Splunk.
Priya (sales-eng): Customer asked whether synthesizing IDs creates PII risk. Short answer: no — request_id already present and redaction still applies. We'll provide a config snapshot showing REDWOOD_REDACT_FIELDS for SOC.
Theo (infra): I'll add a POC checklist: header-echo smoke test, nginx access_log check, forwarder remap/synth, monitor forwarder_429_rate > 5/min alert.
Jordan (solutions): Customer confirmed post-change: traces correlate now. Closing loop — thanks all :white_check_mark:
